comment: Scripted dialogue shown while no model works yet. {{name}} is the guide's name. Options: next (go to node), action (+ onSuccess / onFailure nodes), send (switch to free chat and send this text). Node 'ready' ends the scenario.

hello.say:
Hi, I'm **{{name}}** — I live inside Module Engine and I'll help you set it up.

One thing first: to actually talk (and to run trackers, summaries and the rest), I need a **model**. Right now none is connected.

options.label: I have my own API key

explain.say:
SillyTavern already talks to a model for your chats. Module Engine makes **its own** calls on the side — for trackers, summaries, scene pictures, and for me. Those go to **model connections**: either the same model SillyTavern uses, or a separate one (often cheaper and faster).

The quickest start is to reuse SillyTavern's connection — you can add a separate one later in [Model connections](stme:card:models).

api.say:
Here's how:
```steps
{"title": "Add a model connection", "items": [{"text": "Open Model connections", "anchor": "card:models"}, {"text": "Press + Add connection"}, {"text": "Pick the format (OpenAI-compatible fits most providers), paste the endpoint, API key and model name"}, {"text": "Press Save, then Check now"}]}
```
Tell me when it's saved and I'll check it.

api-failed.say: The check didn't pass — the connection didn't answer. Open [Model connections](stme:card:models): the line under the connection shows the last error. Most often it's the endpoint (it usually ends with **/v1**), the key, or a model name the provider doesn't know.

st-failed.say: SillyTavern's connection didn't answer. Make sure SillyTavern itself is connected (the plug icon at the top) and uses **Chat Completion** or **Text Completion** — then try again. Or set up a separate connection.

ready.say: Connected — now I can really talk. Ask me anything about Module Engine, or pick a start:

options.label: What can Module Engine do?
options.send: What can Module Engine do? Give me a quick tour.
